episodes.text: Tom was a young shepherd boy. Every morning, he led the village sheep up the big green hill. There he sat all day and watched over them. His job was simple. He had to keep the sheep safe and shout for help if a wolf ever came near. But the hill was quiet, and the days were long. The sheep only ate grass and slept in the sun. Tom often felt very bored. He wished that something exciting would happen, just once.

One sleepy afternoon, Tom had a naughty idea. He wanted to see the villagers come running up the hill. He thought it would be great fun to watch. So he jumped to his feet and cupped his hands around his mouth. He took the biggest breath he could. Then he shouted as loudly as he possibly could. "Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is chasing the sheep!" His voice rolled all the way down to the little village below. Tom waited to see what would happen.

Down in the village, the people heard his cry. They dropped everything at once. The baker left his warm bread. The farmer left his plough in the field. They grabbed sticks and brooms and ran up the steep hill as fast as their legs could carry them. They were puffing hard and red in the face. They had come to save Tom and the frightened sheep from the hungry wolf. "Where is it? Where is the wolf?" they called out.

But there was no wolf at all. There was only Tom, rolling on the grass and laughing. "I tricked you! I tricked you all!" he giggled. "You should see your silly faces!" The villagers were not happy. They were cross and tired and out of breath. "That was an unkind trick," said the farmer crossly. "Do not cry wolf when there is no wolf!" Still grumbling, they walked all the way back down the hill. But Tom only smiled and thought it was funny.

For a few days, Tom behaved himself. But soon the hill felt quiet and boring once more. He could not help himself. The same naughty idea popped straight back into his head. He grinned and jumped to his feet again. "Wolf! Wolf!" he yelled with all his might. "Help! A big grey wolf is here!" And just as before, the kind villagers heard him. They dropped their work and hurried up the hill, ready to chase the wolf away and save the poor sheep.

When they reached the top, puffing and tired, they found no wolf. There was only Tom, laughing even harder than before. Now the villagers were truly angry. An old, wise woman shook her head slowly. "Listen to me, Tom," she said. "A boy who tells lies will not be believed. One day you may tell the truth, and still no one will come to help you." But Tom did not listen to her. He thought the old woman was being very silly.

The very next afternoon, the sky grew grey and dark. The sheep were eating quietly when something moved at the edge of the deep forest. Two yellow eyes glowed in the shadows between the trees. Then out crept a real wolf, large and grey and very hungry. It stared at the soft, woolly sheep and licked its lips. Tom's heart began to pound in his chest. This was not a trick. This time the danger was real, and Tom was very frightened.

Tom jumped up and screamed with all his might. "Wolf! Wolf! Please help! There is a real wolf!" Down in the village, the people heard him shouting again. But they only shook their heads and sighed. "That naughty boy is playing his silly trick once more," they said. So nobody came up the hill. The wolf rushed forward, and the sheep scattered across the grass in fear. Poor Tom learned his lesson that day. Nobody believes a liar, even when he tells the truth.
